NEW YORK — October 27, 2026 — Ripple, the leading provider of blockchain solutions across traditional and digital finance, and BNY (NYSE: BNY), a global financial services company, today announced an expansion of their strategic collaboration to broaden institutional digital asset custody capabilities and explore new institutional use cases for blockchain technology, including tokenized trade finance.
The collaboration brings together Ripple’s digital asset solutions and the XRP Ledger (XRPL), a public blockchain, with BNY’s scale, servicing model and digital capabilities.
Building on BNY’s role as primary reserve custodian for Ripple’s stablecoin, RLUSD, and its custody relationship with Ripple Prime, BNY now supports XRP, the native digital asset of the XRP Ledger, and RLUSD on its Digital Asset Custody platform. BNY’s platform is designed to provide institutional clients with secure digital asset custody within the governance, controls and resiliency of its broader servicing model, giving eligible clients a seamless way to safekeep, hold and transfer digital assets.
BNY intends to broaden its support for tokenized assets and investment products issued on the XRPL as institutional use cases on the ledger continue to develop and work with Ripple to enable BNY clients to mint and redeem RLUSD directly through BNY.* Both initiatives aim to support more efficient payments, settlement and collateral workflows over time.
Ripple and BNY also intend to advance tokenized trade finance on the XRPL, subject to client requirements.
As a first step toward this ambition, Ripple and BNY are exploring a supply chain finance initiative with C2FO, a global platform for working capital, focused on expanding investor access to the asset class.
*All references to intended future product plans are subject to final BNY and regulatory approvals.

NEW YORK, June 29, 2026 — BNY (NYSE: BNY), a global financial services company, today announced an expanded relationship with Circle Internet Group, Inc. (NYSE: CRCL) as part of new stablecoin enablement capabilities for institutional clients. Circle USDC will be the first stablecoin on BNY’s Digital Asset Custody platform, enabling BNY clients to store, transfer, mint and burn USDC.
This launch expands BNY’s role as primary custodian of USDC reserves. BNY clients can now hold USDC in their digital asset custody wallets at BNY, and through BNY they can instruct Circle to convert (“mint”) U.S. dollars into USDC and to redeem (“burn”) USDC for U.S. dollars.
“BNY has always been where institutional finance moves first, and making USDC the first stablecoin included in their new offering reflects the regulatory rigor Circle has built into USDC from day one,” said Kash Razzaghi, Chief Commercial Officer at Circle. “This is the next chapter in a longstanding relationship that now gives BNY clients connectivity between on-chain and traditional assets, within the infrastructure they already trust.”

Darkfost2026-11-05
418.5M XRP leave Binance in one day, the biggest Outflow in 9 months
On November 4, 418.5 million XRP were withdrawn from Binance, compared with 315 million on October 29. That represents roughly $540 million, making it the largest outflow day in the past 9 months.
Historically, such withdrawals are often read as a sign of accumulation, but they do not guarantee an upward move, and part of it could also be due to internal movements within the platform.

November 5, 2026
About 280 million XRP entered Binance in just 48 hours, marking a sudden increase in the exchange’s holdings following the Oct. 29 security breach.
Between Nov. 3 and 5, the world’s largest crypto exchange saw its XRP reserves rise from 2.35 billion to 2.63 billion tokens, an increase of 11.9%.
Meanwhile, large-transfer netflows on Binance moved from an outflow of 226 million XRP on Oct. 29 to an inflow of 273 million XRP by Nov. 4. This represents a reversal of roughly 500 million XRP in net movement in less than a week.
The tokens could have come from open-market purchases, over-the-counter (OTC) deals, or transfers between Binance’s internal wallets. However, the exchange has not confirmed which of these explains the increase. As a result, the source of the additional XRP remains unknown.

06 November 2026, 09:52 UTC
About $540 million worth of XRP left Binance in a single day this week. Yet, the price has dropped 7.66% over the past 24 hours to $1.21, according to BeInCrypto Markets.
Coins are leaving the exchange, but buyers have not stepped in to push the price higher. US spot XRP exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have also logged zero net flows for 3 straight sessions.
SoSoValue data shows US spot XRP ETFs recorded zero net flows on November 3, 4, and 5. That quiet stretch included the day of the Binance outflow.
October brought only $18.8 million in net inflows, down from $121.4 million in September.

XRP Insights ETF tracker, accessed 2026-11-06. Data generated 2026-11-06T19:31:50.641Z; data_as_of 2026-11-05.
On Thu, Nov 5, 2026, US XRP ETFs (the 6 spot funds plus BITW) recorded net inflows of 110,214 XRP (≈ $131.2K at that day's XRP price). Combined holdings ended the day at 1.20 billion XRP, with $1.54 billion in net assets.
Latest week net flow: Nov 2–5, 2026, four trading days: -149,487 XRP.
Daily flow = change in each fund's issuer-reported XRP holdings versus the previous trading day. Changes smaller than 100 XRP are treated as rounding noise (0). Flows for GXRP are withheld (flow_status = excluded) across the whole history, matching the XRP Insights dashboard. GXRP's issuer page blocked automated reads from 2026-09-02 to 2026-09-28, so its holdings froze and a four-week catch-up landed on a single day; holdings and AUM for this fund remain in totals.
BITW is a multi-asset index fund; only its XRP position is counted, so its holdings also move with index rebalancing. Changes in holdings caused by anything other than creations/redemptions, such as BITW index rebalancing or fees paid in XRP, are counted as flow.
Settlement timing: issuers publish a session's holdings overnight to the next morning, and some publish a day later. The evening row carries forward previous values and is re-settled the next morning, so the latest row can change and a fund's creation can appear one trading day late.

findings.statement: BNY and Ripple announced a direct strategic collaboration. BNY states it is primary reserve custodian for RLUSD, has a custody relationship with Ripple Prime, and now supports XRP and RLUSD on its Digital Asset Custody platform.
limits: Custody does not prove BNY or its clients bought XRP.
BNY's stated future RLUSD mint/redeem capability through BNY is subject to final BNY and regulatory approvals.
The tokenized trade-finance initiative with C2FO is exploratory and subject to client requirements.

findings.statement: BNY and Circle separately announced an expanded USDC relationship; BNY is primary custodian of USDC reserves and offers institutional clients USDC custody and mint/burn instructions through Circle.
limits: A shared BNY service-provider relationship is not evidence of a direct Circle-Ripple partnership, common ownership, or coordinated stablecoin issuance.

findings.statement: BNY's press release refers to future payments, settlement and collateral workflows for tokenized assets, but does not state that XRP itself is accepted as collateral or that an XRP-backed credit line is live.
limits: Do not convert general collateral language into an XRP collateral feature.

findings.statement: CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost reports 418.5M XRP withdrawn from Binance on Nov 4; The Crypto Basic reports aggregate Binance XRP reserves rising from 2.35B to 2.63B from Nov 3 to Nov 5 and large-transfer netflow turning positive by Nov 4.
limits: One is a reported one-day withdrawal amount; the other is an aggregate reserve balance/large-transfer series across different windows and possibly different wallet labels.
Internal Binance transfers, wallet reclassification, timing, reserve replenishment and external deposits remain competing explanations.
The source of the reported 280M XRP reserve increase is explicitly unknown; do not infer purchases or accumulation.

findings.statement: BeInCrypto citing SoSoValue reports zero net flows for US spot XRP ETFs on Nov 3, 4 and 5. XRP Insights reports +110,214 XRP on Nov 5 across six spot funds plus BITW, while its methodology excludes GXRP from flow totals and counts BITW index-sleeve changes.
limits: The datasets do not share an identical fund universe or documented calculation method.
The direct SoSoValue endpoint linked by BeInCrypto returned HTTP 403 in this retrieval, so the zero-flow claim was not independently reproduced from primary data.
XRP Insights computes flows from holdings deltas, not issuer-reported creations/redemptions; BITW rebalancing/fees can appear as flow, and issuer reporting can lag one day.
Do not average the two claims or admit either as a clean predictive feature without per-fund reconciliation.
